questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
Passing poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.
Following the car in front of you very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to move through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you spot dangerous situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with reckless, careless, inattentive, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that may affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
Fix the problem when you have the money.
Drive slowly instead.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the problem as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any problem that affects safe driving must be fixed right away. Fix problems before you drive.

questions.question: An approaching train is close or moving fast enough to be a danger. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Do not cross the tracks until the train passes completely.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find a different route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train passes completely.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you cannot cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: A car is tailgating you on a multilane highway. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to match the speed of the car behind you.
Move to another lane to let the car pass.
Slow down but stay in your lane.
Let the driver pass and then tailgate them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane to let the car pass.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you on a multilane road, move to the right lane. The left lane should be used only to pass slower traffic.

questions.question: You see railroad crossing signals flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train and then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs, such as a lowered gate or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: When can you proceed through a stop sign intersection with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for other traffic
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
After you stop at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian signals you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: How can you help prevent a car from hitting you from behind?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Let your car slow down before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stopping suddenly makes it hard for cars behind you to stop in time. Release the gas pedal first to let your car slow. Then apply steady brake pressure so your brake lights come on and your car stops smoothly.

questions.question: You are in the right lane and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for cars in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following other cars too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Look for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed all the time.
Only drives on familiar roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: All drivers can be distracted. A good defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems before they happen.

questions.question: When should you use one-hand steering?

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
When avoiding a hazard at high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing up or using controls like signals, radio, or windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When backing up or using controls like signals, radio, or windshield wipers.
questions.explanation: Use one hand to steer only when backing up or when you need to reach for vehicle controls like wipers, signals, or lights.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus has flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is out.

questions.question: How can you prevent alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say "no thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving crashes is to decide not to drive before you drink. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it hard to make safe decisions once you have started drinking.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment depends on:

options.text: Whether you drink beer instead of wine.
Whether you drink wine instead of beer.
Whether you drink hard cider or mixed drinks.
How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol hurts your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Look over your shoulder through the rear window.
Use only a backup camera.
Put your head out of the driver's window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, turn your head and look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors or a backup camera.

questions.question: How can you prevent highway hypnosis?

options.text: Start your drive well-rested.
Stop regularly, even if you do not feel tired.
Keep your eyes moving.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Long drives can cause boredom and highway hypnosis. To avoid this, start your trip well-rested. Stop regularly even if you are not tired. Keep your eyes scanning to avoid getting tired from staring at one spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means no U-turns are allowed. Do not make a U-turn where you see this sign.

questions.question: When should you use hand-over-hand steering?

options.text: When turning the wheel during normal driving.
When avoiding a hazard at high speed.
When turning the wheel at low speeds.
When backing up or using controls like signals, radio, or windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: When turning the wheel at low speeds.
questions.explanation: Use hand-over-hand steering when turning at low speeds, such as at an intersection or when parking. Place your left hand between 8 and 9 o'clock on the wheel and your right hand between 3 and 4 o'clock.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at an intersection with multiple lanes. Oncoming traffic is blocking your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane of traffic as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and you can turn safely.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats if they are too small for regular safety belts. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Children must always be properly fastened in a seat.

questions.question: When should you use your parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park.
Only when you park on a hill.
Only when you park on a busy street.
Only when you park in a parking lot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park.
questions.explanation: Use your parking brake every time you park, whether your car is manual or automatic and whether the ground is flat or hilly.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use only your parking lights.
Use only your headlights.
Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights when stopped on a road at night. Make sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with its lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes if possible to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes if possible to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. If you cannot change lanes safely or there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop at an emergency scene.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and proceed carefully at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light.
A flashing red light.
A solid yellow light.
A solid red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be cautious, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A solid yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.

options.text: Flashing yellow.
Solid green.
Solid red.
Flashing red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Solid red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means a solid red light will appear next.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm downward, they are signaling that they are stopping. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this signal.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or gradually slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times a minute to spot tailgaters or fast-approaching vehicles. If someone is following too closely, slow down gradually and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You come to a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, give the right-of-way to other traffic, and go only when it is safe.
